Evidence behind the bouts of illness

Source: R/bouts.r
bout_evidence.Rd

bouts_of_illness gives one row per bout. The evidence it rests on is in the list returned here, from the same reconstruction. The bout membership is the same as in bouts_of_illness(x). Date policies affect selected boundaries, not the original report evidence.

Usage

bout_evidence(
  x,
  start.date = c("earliest", "last"),
  missing.start = c("missing", "first.report"),
  inverted.dates = c("keep", "clear", "reset.end"),
  expand.days = TRUE,
  precedence = c("dates", "continuation", "report.date"),
  unresolved = c("fill", "missing"),
  chronic = c("none", "duration"),
  chronic.days = NULL
)

Arguments

x

the data to extract bouts from, as for bouts_of_illness

start.date, missing.start, inverted.dates

Date policies as in bouts_of_illness; start.date defaults to "earliest" in both. Evidence defaults to leaving an unreported onset missing; the summary interface defaults to the first report. These policies do not replace the original report evidence.

expand.days

whether to expand established illness intervals to individual days. Set FALSE for interval matching without daily expansion.

precedence, unresolved

Bout formation and treatment of a bout with no reported end date, as in bouts_of_illness.

chronic, chronic.days

Chronic report rule as in bouts_of_illness.

Value

a list of data tables: bouts, reports, intervals and days

Details

reports has a row for each symptomatic report that belongs to a bout, with the bout it belongs to, the dates it reported (report.start, report.end) and the days of illness it supports, first.day to last.day. The column basis says how: "reported" (start and end date given, the end counted no later than the report), "still.ill" (continuing illness from the start date to the report), "still.ill.unknown.onset" (continuing illness with no start date: only the day of the report is established, and neither the onset nor the recovery) or "unresolved" (no usable interval, so no day).

days has a row for each day of illness the reports establish, with source "reported" for days within a reported or continuing interval and "report.date" for days established only by a report of continuing illness without a start date. Days between the intervals of a bout are included with source "within.bout": illness persists between established illness days of the same bout. Selected fallback boundaries are not used to establish illness. The intervals table contains the first and last established day per bout without daily expansion.

bouts has a row per bout with dates selected by the supplied date policies, and onset.known and recovery.known, which say whether any report of the bout gave a matching start or end date for the selected boundary. The columns onset.source and recovery.source distinguish reported dates, missing boundaries and first/last-report fallbacks. The columns n.reports and the case definitions follow: the symptom columns of all reports of a bout are combined (a symptom counts if any report has it, the onset if any report records it as sudden) and the definitions applied to the result. The classification belongs to the bout and does not say that the symptoms were present together on a day. The definitions are ili, ili.fever, ili.self, resp.symptoms (ARI) and the others of aggregate_symptoms that are in the data; onset.conflict records conflicting explicit onset answers; onset keeps the highest-precedence onset answer ("sudden", "not.sudden", "dont_know", "not.answered", "no.question"). Where the columns that a definition is built from are not in the data, it is positive if any report of the bout is.

Examples

dt <- extract_data(simulated_data, years = 2013:2014)
#> Warning: The contact and symptom surveys are joined by report date, which pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report however long before it was filed, and (with 'unsuccessful.join') drops symptom reports that have none. To link contacts to illness, extract them separately and use contact_illness().
#> Warning: The contact and symptom surveys are joined by report date, which pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report however long before it was filed, and (with 'unsuccessful.join') drops symptom reports that have none. To link contacts to illness, extract them separately and use contact_illness().
evidence <- bout_evidence(dt)
head(evidence$days)
#>    participant_id  season  bout        day   source
#>             <int>  <char> <int>     <Date>   <char>
#> 1:              2 2013/14     1 2014-02-09 reported
#> 2:              2 2013/14     1 2014-02-10 reported
#> 3:              2 2013/14     1 2014-02-11 reported
#> 4:              2 2013/14     1 2014-02-12 reported
#> 5:              2 2013/14     1 2014-02-13 reported
#> 6:              2 2013/14     1 2014-02-14 reported
